full_judgment:
2. The appellant before us as plaintiff filed the suit seeking eviction of the defendants on 2 grounds, namely (1) default in payment of rent and (2) bona fide requirement of the suit premises for the plaintiff s own occupation. 

 3. The plaintiff averred that he purchased the suit premises from Zaish Khan and Mahbubunnessa by Kabala dated 20-6-1997 and 15-7-1997. Prior to his purchase, the defendants were already tenant the premises, who had knowledge of the transfer of ownership. The plaintiff after purchasing the property asked the defendants to vacate the property and the latter recognising the former as the landlord, asked for 6 months' time, and the plaintiff oblige, as they agreed to pay the rent for the said 6 months period @ Taka 300 per month. Though the defendants paid rent for the months of August, September and October, they paid no more and at the end of the said 6 months, they kept staying in the premises on different pretexts. In view of the defendants' said default and failure to vacate the premises the plaintiff served upon them a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act on 28-2-1999, terminating the tenancy, which was received by the defendants. 

 4. In their reply, the defendants did not only express their refusal to vacate, but also denied that they were plaintiffs tenant. It was mentioned in the notice that the tenancy would come to an end on 31-3-1999 after which the defendants would be treated as trespassers, and would be liable to pay Taka 50 for each day's overstay. The notice also contained a demand for the payment of Taka 800 as arrear rent. The suit was then filed in view of the defendants' negative response. 

 6. On having lost their legal battle at the trial Court, the defendants moved the High Court Division, which, in making the Rule absolute and thereby set-aside the trial Court's judgment observing that the trial Court was in error in decreeing the suit notwithstanding that there is nothing in the trial Court's judgment that tenant landlord relationship existed between the plaintiff and the defendants; that the trial Court misread Exhibits-13, 14 and 15, in that there is nothing in these Exhibits to reveal that the defendants admitted the plaintiff as their landlord. It also observed that the trial Court also mis-constructed PW 1's deposition in that the said PW in cross-examination admitted that he did not produce any document to show that there is any landlord-tenant relationship between the parties to the suit. It also observed that the defendants succeeded to show by adducing oral and documentary evidence that their lather purchased the suit premises by a kabala dated 16-10-1969 and also that as there was a claim and a counterclaim, as to the title of the suit land, the Small Causes Court should not have proceeded to try the suit for ejectment, rather it should have returned the plaint for presentation before the appropriate Court. It added that the plaintiff failed to prove the fact of default in payment of rent and land lord-tenant relationship. 

 7. The plaintiff then filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 83 of 2005 and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner: — 

 "I. That there being an admission by the defendants as stated by him as DW 3 defendant No. 1 in the suit that the defendants were tenants under the original owner from whom the plaintiff has purchased the disputed property. 

 II. That the admission of the defendants as tenant under the original landlord from whom the plaintiff purchased has also being made in Exhibit 15 in the Complaint Case No. 127 of 1997 in the Court of the local Magistrate. 

 IV. That the plaintiffs have produced their documents of purchase of the suit property from original landlord along with other documents in support of their claim of title. 

 V. That the SCC Judge having decided the prima facie title of the plaintiff on consideration of the documents as were produced by the parties and incidentally decided the title of the plaintiff and also found that defendants being defaulter and decreed the suit for eviction of the defendants. 

 8. As we took up the appeal for hearing Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate for the appellants, submitted that there being an admission by the defendants as stated by him DW's 1 and 3 to the effect that they were tenants, and that as ext-15 in the complaint case No. 1278 of 1997 in the Court of a local Magistrate shows the defendants were tenants under the original landlord, from whom the plaintiff purchased the premises, the Small Causes Court was right to pass the judgment and the decree. 

 9. He went on to add that the defendants utterly failed .o produce original title deed dated 16-10-1969, while the plaintiff succeeded to produce documents to prove their claimed purchase from the original landlord, along with other supporting documents to establish their claimed title. 

 13. Documents produced by the plaintiff to show his claimed purchase, had also remained unimpeached while the defendants have failed to produce their claimed documents in original form.
